# Skew quadruple of order 89 over the cyclic group Z_89, from a three-pool join with a fixed skew block. It gives a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356.
# Run on one machine (16 threads, 28 GB), 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-22. The search code (pg2.c, pgu.c, tj7s.c) is not in the repository; this file is the run record.
# Method. The skew first block A is fixed in advance and is invariant under the multiplier group H of order 11 generated by 2 modulo 89. A plan gives, for each of the
# other three blocks and each nonzero lag, a window of allowed periodic autocorrelation values, chosen so that the four values can sum to zero. A local search
# collects rows inside the windows of each block (hits), which form three pools, and the pools are joined exactly: every triple of rows, one per pool and up to the
# action of H, whose autocorrelations sum with that of A to zero at every nonzero lag is reported.
# This is a sampling search: the pools hold a small part of the rows inside the windows, so the result is one solution, not a census, and it says nothing about how
# many classes exist.
# Round 1 (narrower windows, plan n2: block 0 windows {-7..1} and {-3..5}, block 2 windows {-3..5}; block 1 as below): 12339248, 80577329 and 12280944 hits; the
# join of all 1227 depth-4 subtrees found no solution.
# Round 2 (the plan below, whose windows contain those of round 1): 31000000 and 43000000 new hits for blocks 0 and 2 under the plan below and 3600000 new hits
# for block 1, generated in about 10 minutes on 16 threads, joined together with the round-1 hits.
#   pool 0: row 3, 43455792 hits
#   pool 1: row 11, 84177329 hits
#   pool 2: row 15, 55280944 hits
# The join was cut into slices by the first two key digits so that it fits in memory. Slices 0,0 and 0,3 are empty; slices 0,1 and 0,2 finished with no solution
# (2.36e+08 and 1.07e+04 nodes). Slice 1,0 (169939387, 79634320 and 174136422 distinct keys) reported the solution below within 3 hours 46 minutes of its start;
# when this record was written that slice was still running (224 depth-4 subtrees done, 7.22e+09 nodes, 14589 s on 16 threads) and the later slices had not
# started, so the number of solutions in these pools is not yet known.
# Checks of the solution, in code separate from the search: entries +-1; A skew (a_0 = 1, a_i = -a_{89-i}); the four periodic autocorrelations sum to zero at
# every nonzero lag; the Goethals-Seidel matrix G of order 356 satisfies G G^T = 356 I and G + G^T = 2 I. Row sums -11, 1, -3, 15 after the board's
# normalisation (121 + 1 + 9 + 225 = 356).
# Status of the order. 356 is the smallest order for which the existence of a skew-Hadamard matrix was undecided according to arXiv:2301.02751, and it is the first
# of the open orders in baselines/skew-gaps.json (arXiv:2411.18897v2). A search of current sources on 2026-11-22 (arXiv listings to 2026-11-18, the SageMath
# list of unknown skew orders, public repositories of skew-Hadamard matrices) found no skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356; that is a report of the search, not a
# proof of priority.
# plan file:

#   11
